g.text: FROM STRATEGY TO A REPEATABLE DECISION
Why does the right direction for the company not
always produce the same result locally?
Management sets a clear direction, for example: “high availability with fewer days
inventory.” At the strategy level, everything looks logical. But locally, it turns into
The same policy is executed differently, and
the company gets different business results.
The policy is converted into specific rules,
and every unit makes the same decision
A company direction does not yet constitute a system.
For a strategy to produce the same result, it needs an execution
mechanism — common rules, parameters, and process.
Scale does not begin when a company opens its hundredth pharmacy. Scale
begins when the right decision can be repeated the same way one hundred
